newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada's Noel says Canada dlr undervalued.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada's Noel says Canada dlr undervalued.

text.p: Bank of Canada deputy governor Timothy Noel said on Wednesday that the Canadian dollar remains undervalued in the medium term.
"The fundamental situation is that in the medium term, the Canadian dollar is undervalued," Noel told reporters after a luncheon speech.

Noel said Canada would not be able to sustain its interest rate differential with U.S. rates if the Canadian dollar were not undervalued. "People aren't going to hold Canadian dollars at lower interest rates if they think the Canadian dollar isn't going to appreciate," he said.

Asked whether Canada could buck any move to increase U.S. interest rates, Noel said that would depend on U.S. economic conditions prompting such a rise and on prevailing economic conditions in Canada.

"It depends on the circumstances of the rise. If it's because the U.S. economy is growing at a very rapid rate, that could have an impact on growth in Canada and we may need to follow. On the other hand, if Canada still remains weak, there may be no reason for us to move," Noel said.
"I think the markets think that Canada could deal with an increase in (U.S.) interest rates without moving," he said.
Earlier Wednesday, U.S. central bank chief Alan Greenspan voiced concerns about U.S. inflation, warning that the Federal Reserve could not rule out a "pre-emptive" policy tightening.
Noel said the "balance of risks" in the U.S. and Canadian economies are quite different, with the U.S. economy being at full capacity and Canada still having about three percent headroom.
Noel said he expects Canada's gross domestic product to grow by four percent in 1997.
"We think that things are poised for a good strong year in 1997," Noel said.
